title: First snow, Blatt's Palm Garden and boxing with Muggsy
summary: He plays the first set, goes wild in his first snow, meets Jack Pettis, Frank Snyder, Elmer Schoebel and Muggsy at Blatt's, and is made to box Muggsy; then the move to Lincoln Gardens and a Streckfus boat offer.

bands.name: Ray Miller's Black and White Melody Boys

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Uh, Rag Baby, Paul, myself and Tramonist, piano player. I just can't recall the piano player. Oh God, yeah. So, uh, we played the first set and went over pretty good and ragged. And the boss, uh, Stein was very happy. So I happened to go outside and somebody said, it's snowing. So I wanted to see snow and it was snowing like the diggings. You've never seen it before. I never seen it. I've seen it on Christmas cards, but I thought it was fictional. So I start rolling around in the snow and clowning and throwing snowballs, never having a ball. So the boss comes on and he says, you're on. I says, to hell with the job. I says, I quit. I didn't have a dime in my pocket. I was so happy. So the guy says, well, all right, have a little fun and then come in and play. So I missed the set and I went back in. And then from that time on, the job was all right. We stayed there all for a good length of time. And then we went to a place called the Lincoln Gardens. And, uh, well, I'm getting a little ahead of my story. When I first came in, uh, uh, after the, uh, what's the name? We went down to Blatt's Palm Garden. That's where I met the famous Jack Pettis on the, on the C. Miller saxophone, Frank Snyder, and Elmer Schoble. And then Muggsy could only play one tune at that time. A number called Sensation. So these two racketeers, uh, bouncers and hoods, they, uh, after, uh, Jack and, uh, Elmer introduced Muggsy and I. I played, Muggsy sat in, we played. So after this, after the night was over, they took us over to an athletic club. And they made us put the boxing gloves on. I said, man, I don't want to hurt this man. I just met him. I just said, hello, how do you do this? So they made us do it. You know how they do in Chicago. They made us do it. So we boxed for about two hours. I knocked Muggsy down. Muggsy knocked me down. I got a broken thumb. I broke on Muggsy's head. Then Muggsy sprang out and he went with, uh, Miller's Black and White Melody Boys. And that's when, after we played the Lincoln, we went, after we played the Camel Gardens, we went to the Lincoln Gardens on Lincoln and Madison. That's where, uh, Pettis got the, uh, idea. He didn't get the idea. There was a telegram sent to go to work on the Streckfus boats in St. Louis. There was, uh, what's the Clannet players? Uh, um, Palazano. Oh, yeah.
